title: Light Armored Reconnaissance Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O #
raw_text:
4.     MOS 0313, Light Armored Reconnaissance Marine (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC PP&O
#

    a. Summary. The Light Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Marine is an
infantry Marine skilled in armored reconnaissance. In addition to basic
infantry skills, they are knowledgeable in armored reconnaissance and
surveillance, and armored security missions in support of the MAGTF to gain
information on the enemy and terrain. LAR Marines provide gunnery and
weapons skills for the employment of the 25mm Chain Gun, the Coaxial and
Pintle-Mounted 7.62mm Machineguns and thermal optics on the LAV-25 variant.
LAR Marines receive advanced training as vehicle operators, LAV-25 Gunners,
LAR Vehicle Commanders and LAR Master Gunners. Non-Commissioned Officers are
assigned as LAV-25 Gunners and Vehicle Commanders.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess a height of 65 to 75 inches.

            (2) Must have WS-B water survival qualification.

            (3) Must possess a CL score of 90 or GT score of 90 or higher.

        (4) Must possess normal color vision, normal depth perception and
visual acuity of 20/200 (correctable to 20/20).

        (5) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.

        (6) Must possess the psychological and physiological qualifications
required for licensing as an ordnance vehicle operator (see reference (cz)).




                                          3-23                       Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



        (7) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF
assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit
training.

        (8) Must have a valid state driver’s license and a past driving
record appropriate for issue of SF-86 as evidenced by a search of the
National Driver Register.

        (9) Must be qualified as Basic Infantry Marine having completed
training at Schools of Infantry East or West, at the infantry training
battalion (ITB) as a 0311. Marines seeking an MOS lateral move (LAT move) to
the 0313 MOS are required to complete ITB training if they have not been
previously held an Infantry MOS of 0311, 0321, 0331, 0341, or 0352.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Infantry Marine Course (M03RG34) SOI Camp Lejeune,
NC or (M10RG32) SOI Camp Pendleton, CA.

        (2) Complete the Light Armored Reconnaissance Marine Course (LARMC)
(M10H2F2), Camp Pendleton, CA.

        (3) Must attain WS-I water survival intermediate qualification prior
to completion of the Light Armored Reconnaissance Marine Course (LARMC).

        (4) Sergeants must complete the Light Armored Reconnaissance
Commander Course (M10H3V2).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (de), Light Armored Reconnaissance (LAR) Training and Readiness
(T&R) Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Infantry 55-3016.

            (2) Armored Assault Vehicle Crew Members 55-3013.

            (3) First-Line Supervisor of Weapons Specialist/Crew Members 55-2012.

            (4) Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

        (5) First-Line Supervisors of all Other Tactical Operations
Specialist 55-2013.

        (6) Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons
Specialists and Crew Members, All Other 55-3019.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Reconnaissance Marine, 0321.

            (2) Ground Operations Specialist, 8711.

# The 0313 MOS is no longer assigned to SNCOs within the LAR OccFld. LAR
OccFld SNCOs who have not completed the appropriate formal school for their
current grade will maintain their previous PMOS until attrition or they have
met the requirements for their current grade. SNCOs who have not



                                         3-24                        Enclosure (1)
 3110                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L



matriculated to their PMOS of 0363 or 0393 are not eligible for retention or
promotion until they have completed the grade appropriate formal school.
They may request an extension in lieu of reenlistment for the express purpose
of gaining sufficient obligated service time to meet the 0363/ 0393
requirement.
common_text: In addition to the Infantry Officer, Marine Gunner, and Infantry Unit Leader, the 03 Infantry Occupational Field is comprised of the following specialties rifleman, light armor vehicle marine, reconnaissance marine, machine gunner, mortarman, and antitank missile gunner. Regardless of specialty, Infantry Marines are primarily employed in units from the team to regimental-level in order to locate, close with, and destroy the enemy in all environments and weather conditions, during both the day and night. Excluding Light Armored Reconnaissance Units, Infantry Marines are principally trained to operate light and fast on foot. Infantry units are capable of multiple methods of entry and insertion, embarking aboard and fighting from helicopters, assault amphibious vehicles, motorized tactical vehicles, ultra-light tactical vehicles, and small boats. As the principal component of a Marine Air-Ground Task Force's ground combat element, Infantry Marines must be able to operate effectively in austere and distributed environments characterized by friction, uncertainty, and chaos. All Infantry Marines must be physically dominant and masters of small arms marksmanship, tactical combat casualty care, and battle drills in every operating environment. Infantry units must be comprised of Marines proficient in the employment of demolitions, rockets, machineguns, mortars, and missile systems and capable of directing supporting arms. Infantry Marines must also be proficient in field craft and capable of employing unmanned systems, limited information warfare, and non-lethal systems.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
